title: What they said at the time

clips.q: Kiddie City is an experience like the Taj Mahal by moonlight. It’s a Grand Canyon of toys.
clips.who: **Jim Myers**, Democrat and Chronicle, December 1979, as quoted in the paper’s 2017 retrospective[^28]

clips.q: There is nothing wrong with specialty toy retailing.
clips.who: **Walter Peterson**, analyst, Fahnestock & Company, The New York Times, Feb 25, 1982[^1]
**Michael Vastola**, asked why Kiddie City had not been in New York before, The New York Times, Nov 13, 1988[^10]

clips.q: We continue to have a desire to acquire Lionel but are deeply troubled by the decline in the operating performance of the business.
We’re viewing this as a situation to revive the company.
clips.who: **Michael J. Vastola**, on the second Chapter 11 filing, The New York Times, Jun 15, 1991[^16]

clips.q: What you have here is purely a toy reseller who, unfortunately, could not compete against Toys ‘R’ Us.
clips.who: **David Liebowitz**, analyst, American Securities, UPI, Jun 14, 1991[^17]

clips.q: Toy manufacturers have been extremely patient with the two companies, and they’ve just about run out of patience.
clips.who: **Gary Jacobson**, analyst, Kidder, Peabody, on Lionel and Child World, The New York Times, Jun 12, 1992[^20]

clips.q: There were a few good sales, but Lionel is generally more expensive than Walmart or other stores.
clips.who: **Nadene Dahlstrom**, shopper at a Utah closing sale, Deseret News, Oct 22, 1991[^18]
**Sally Smith**, analyst, Alex. Brown & Sons, on the January 1993 closings, Discount Store News[^23]

clips.q: Everyone was hoping we would weather the storm.
clips.who: **Tim Gnap**, store manager, Bel Air, Md., The Baltimore Sun, Jun 6, 1993[^27]
